description: Scotch Bonnet Peppers are a hot pepper cultivar shaped like a hat. They have a rating of 100,000–350,000 Scoville units, making them much spicier than jalapenos. Scotch Bonnets are sweeter and stouter than habaneros and used in Caribbean cuisine. Sweet varieties are known as Cachucha Peppers. The fruit is green when young and red when ripe. Scotch Bonnets are often harvested when yellow-orange. Plants grown with less water will produce hotter peppers.
sowing_method: Direct seed (and transplant after hardening off) or seedlings

data_sources.notes: growth_habit='upright' inferred by Ollama (no Trefle growth_habit data (no cached match or null field)); reasoning: Scotch Bonnet Peppers grow as an upright bush from the ground.
life_cycle='annual' inferred by Ollama; reasoning: Scotch Bonnet Peppers are typically grown as annuals in Belgium due to their sensitivity to cold temperatures.
edible_parts=['fruit'] inferred by Ollama; reasoning: Scotch Bonnet Peppers are primarily eaten for their fruit.
